One is a real code fix in tt-mlir; the other two are how the compiler has to be driven. None of them touched the op mapping — that was already correct.</font>' style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=17;fontColor=#0f172a;" vertex="1" parent="1"><mxGeometry x="40" y="34" width="1780" height="64" as="geometry" /></mxCell><mxCell id="h0" value="<b>1. The system descriptor lied about Quasar's data formats</b>" style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=14;fontColor=#0f172a;" vertex="1" parent="1"><mxGeometry x="40" y="116" width="1780" height="26" as="geometry" /></mxCell><mxCell id="b00" value="<b>BEFORE — one list for every arch</b><br><br><font style="font-size:9px">Quasar advertised Wormhole's 13 formats,</font><br><font style="font-size:9px">including bfp_bf8 / bfp_bf4 / u16 / u32,</font><br><font style="font-size:9px">none of which Quasar can run.</font><br>&nbsp;<br><font style="font-size:9px">Both the mock AND the live builder had the</font><br><font style="font-size:9px">same hardcoded list, so they agreed with</font><br><font style="font-size:9px">each other and the bug was invisible.</font><br><font style="font-size:9px">The live builder even said so:</font><br><font style="font-size:9px"> “temporary place-holder value to be</font><br><font style="font-size:9px"> replaced by API value”</font>" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#fbe4e4;strokeColor=#d05c5c;fontColor=#5c1010;align=left;verticalAlign=top;spacingLeft=10;spacingTop=4;fontSize=11;" vertex="1" parent="1"><mxGeometry x="40" y="150" width="560" height="210" as="geometry" /></mxCell><mxCell id="b01" value='<b>CHANGE — ask tt-metal instead</b><br><font style="font-size:9px;color:#5b6472">tt-mlir: TTCoreOpsTypes.cpp:85 + system_desc.cpp:181</font><br><br><font style="font-size:9px">tt::is_data_format_supported(fmt, arch)</font><br><font style="font-size:9px"> tt_backend_api_types.hpp:72 (public API)</font><br><font style="font-size:9px"> -&gt; is_supported_quasar()</font><br>&nbsp;<br><font style="font-size:9px">Live builder: enumerate all 13 target types,</font><br><font style="font-size:9px">map each to a tt::DataFormat, keep what that</font><br><font style="font-size:9px">arch admits. No hardcoded list at all.</font><br>&nbsp;<br><font style="font-size:9px">Mock: carry the matching 5 so a device-free</font><br><font style="font-size:9px">compile agrees with the device.</font>' style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#fdf0d5;strokeColor=#d99e2b;fontColor=#4a2f00;align=left;verticalAlign=top;spacingLeft=10;spacingTop=4;fontSize=11;" vertex="1" parent="1"><mxGeometry x="660" y="150" width="560" height="210" as="geometry" /></mxCell><mxCell id="b02" value='<b>AFTER — arch-correct, and self-consistent</b><br><br><font style="font-size:9px">quasar : f32, f16, bf16, u8, si32 (5)</font><br><font style="font-size:9px">wormhole : unchanged (13)</font><br>&nbsp;<br><font style="font-size:9px">num_cbs fixed the same way:</font><br><font style="font-size:9px"> was NUM_CIRCULAR_BUFFERS, an array-sizing</font><br><font style="font-size:9px"> constant = 64 on ANY host build</font><br><font style="font-size:9px"> now hal::get_arch_num_circular_buffers()</font><br><font style="font-size:9px"> -&gt; live Wormhole 64 -&gt; 32 (was wrong!)</font><br>&nbsp;<br><font style="font-size:9px">Verified 4 ways: mock + live, both arches.</font>' style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#e8e2f7;strokeColor=#8b6fc9;fontColor=#2b1a55;align=left;verticalAlign=top;spacingLeft=10;spacingTop=4;fontSize=11;" vertex="1" parent="1"><mxGeometry x="1280" y="150" width="560" height="210" as="geometry" /></mxCell><mxCell id="h1" value="<b>2. Forge emitted f32, which takes a different kernel</b>" style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=14;fontColor=#0f172a;" vertex="1" parent="1"><mxGeometry x="40" y="366" width="1780" height="26" as="geometry" /></mxCell><mxCell id="b10" value='<b>BEFORE — f32 livelocks</b><br><br><font style="font-size:9px">An ONNX graph is float32, so forge emitted</font><br><font style="font-size:9px">f32 tensors and the run hung forever:</font><br>&nbsp;<br><font style="font-size:9px"> pending_tensix = 4</font><br><font style="font-size:9px"> srcA/srcB = valid=1 unpack=1 matrix=0</font><br>&nbsp;<br><font style="font-size:9px">Operands delivered; the math unit never</font><br><font style="font-size:9px">consumed them. The watchdog stays silent by</font><br><font style="font-size:9px">design — the loop keeps retiring</font><br><font style="font-size:9px">instructions, so it is a livelock.</font>' svg.text: Running Add on Quasar: what we changed
Three changes. One is a real code fix in tt-mlir; the other two are how the compiler has to be driven. None of them touched the op
1. The system descriptor lied about Quasar's data formats
BEFORE — one list for every arch
none of which Quasar can run.
Both the mock AND the live builder had the
same hardcoded list, so they agreed with
each other and the bug was invisible.
The live builder even said so:
Live builder: enumerate all 13 target types,
map each to a tt::DataFormat, keep what that
arch admits. No hardcoded list at all.
Mock: carry the matching 5 so a device-free
quasar : f32, f16, bf16, u8, si32 (5)
Verified 4 ways: mock + live, both arches.
2. Forge emitted f32, which takes a different kernel
An ONNX graph is float32, so forge emitted
f32 tensors and the run hung forever:
Operands delivered; the math unit never
consumed them. The watchdog stays silent by
instructions, so it is a livelock.
one line of config — no code change
is_binary_sfpu_op is TRUE for any f32 op
including add, so f32 routes the SFPU
kernel, and bf16 routes the FPU
A different compute path, not a wider one.
f32 still livelocks and is tracked
3. Kernel include paths resolve against the cwd, not TT_METAL_HOME
BEFORE — fails from the forge repo
With bf16 the hang was replaced by a hard,
compute' not found relative to current
paths RELATIVE to the tt-metal root.
Identical upstream, so this is a tt-metal
CONVENTION, not a bug: their suite always
runs from their repo root, so it never bit
them. forge is a different repo.
4 passed in 11 s, run from the forge root.
Why none of this was the op mapping
The mapping was already correct and already being reached: binary.cpp's RUN_ELTWISE_BINARY picks
ttnn::operations::experimental::quasar::binary::add when isQuasar(). Score every op three ways —
(1) does a Quasar op exist, (2) does the runtime dispatch to it, (3) does it run. Only (3) counts,
and (1)+(2) being green is exactly why “add is unmapped” was the wrong diagnosis for weeks.
test_add_bf16 / test_mul_bf16 / test_sub_bf16 / test_div_bf16 -> 4 passed in 11 s, Add PCC 0.999985
test_add_op.py -> 16 passed in 14 s, device-free (5 of them Quasar: lowering, dtype, descriptor contents, Bfp8_b rejection)
No tt-metal pin bump was needed. Open: f32 still livelocks — different kernel path, tracked separately.
